rejected.title: Islamic sexual ethics
card: In Islam, sexual relationships belong within marriage. Marriage is seen as a lawful and committed bond between a husband and wife, and it is linked to companionship, mercy and family life.
Sex outside marriage is taught to be wrong. Islamic teaching also encourages Muslims to avoid situations that could lead towards it.
Modesty (haya) is a value that shapes behaviour, speech and dress. It is taught for both men and women, and Muslims may practise it in different ways.
These teachings draw on the Quran, which Muslims believe is the word of God, and the Hadith, which are reports of the words and actions of the Prophet Muhammad.
rejected.remember: Marriage is the setting for sexual relationships, and modesty guides how Muslims act, speak and dress.

a.q: A Muslim teacher is asked why Islam does not accept sex outside marriage. Which reply best matches Islamic teaching?
opts: Marriage is the lawful, committed bond for intimacy
Marriage is only a legal contract with no moral purpose
Sexual relationships are accepted if both people agree
Sexual relationships are wrong even inside marriage
a.why: Islam places sexual relationships within marriage, which is seen as a lawful and committed bond. Agreement between two people matters, but it does not replace marriage as the setting. The view that sex is wrong even in marriage is also incorrect, since marriage is where it belongs.
a.clue: Which setting does the card call lawful and committed?

b.q: Samira, a Muslim student in Perth, says modesty is only about how women dress. Why is her view incomplete?
opts: Modesty also shapes behaviour and speech, for men too
Modesty is about dress, but it applies to men and women
Modesty covers behaviour and speech, but only for women
Modesty is taught in the Hadith, not in the Quran
b.why: The card says modesty shapes behaviour, speech and dress, and is taught for both men and women. Samira leaves out behaviour, speech and men. The second option is tempting because it corrects only the gender part, but it still treats modesty as dress alone.
b.clue: Check both what modesty covers and who it is taught for.

A student could read it as describing marriage. It needs to say plainly that the bond is outside marriage, for example 'an unmarried committed couple'.

'Modesty shapes dress, and it is taught for men too' correctly names one way Samira's view is incomplete: modesty is not only for women. A careful teacher could defend it as right. The stem should ask for the most complete correction, or this option should be reworded so it is clearly wrong.

proposal.title: Islamic sexual ethics
card: In Islam, sexual relationships belong within marriage. Marriage is seen as a lawful and committed bond between a husband and wife, linked to companionship, mercy and family life.
Sex outside marriage is taught to be wrong. Islamic teaching also encourages Muslims to avoid situations that could lead towards it.
Modesty (haya) is a value that shapes behaviour, speech and dress. It is taught for both men and women, and Muslims may practise it in different ways.
These teachings draw on the Quran, which Muslims believe is the word of God, and the Hadith, which are reports of the words and actions of the Prophet Muhammad.
proposal.remember: Marriage is the setting for sexual relationships, and modesty is a value for both men and women.

a.q: Which statement best explains Islamic teaching on sex outside marriage?
opts: It is wrong, as marriage is the lawful setting for intimacy
It is fine for an unmarried committed couple who consent
It is wrong only if the couple do not plan to marry
It is a private matter that the teaching does not address
a.why: Islam places sexual relationships within marriage, a lawful and committed bond, so sex outside marriage is taught to be wrong. The unmarried committed couple option is tempting, but commitment without marriage is still outside the setting Islam names.
a.clue: Is commitment enough, or does the teaching name a specific bond?

b.q: Samira, a Muslim student in Perth, says modesty is only about how women dress. Which correction best fixes her view?
opts: Modesty shapes behaviour, speech and dress, for men too
Modesty is about dress alone, but it is taught for men too
Modesty shapes behaviour and speech, but mainly for women
Modesty shapes dress, and every Muslim practises it alike
b.why: Modesty shapes behaviour, speech and dress, and it is taught for both men and women. The option saying modesty is about dress alone but taught for men too is tempting, because it fixes who modesty applies to, but it still wrongly limits modesty to dress.
b.clue: Check both what modesty covers and who it is taught for.
